body:
### Describe the bug

When `max()` or `min()` is called with two or more positional arguments, the compiled code evaluates the first argument last: `max(f(1), f(2))` calls `f(2)` and then `f(1)`, and `min(f(3), f(4), f(5))` calls `f(4)`, `f(5)`, then `f(3)`. Python evaluates call arguments from left to right (language reference, [Calls](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#calls) and [Evaluation order](https://docs.python.org/3/reference/expressions.html#evaluation-order)). The returned value is still the right one when the arguments do not affect each other, but their side effects happen in a different order.

### Code to reproduce the behaviour:

```python
# minmax.py
def f(x):
    print('eval', x)
    return x

print(max(f(1), f(2)))
print(min(f(3), f(4), f(5)))
```

Built with `cythonize -i -3 minmax.py`, then `python -c "import minmax"`:

| | output |
|---|---|
| CPython 3.12.13, 3.14.6 | `eval 1`, `eval 2`, `2`, `eval 3`, `eval 4`, `eval 5`, `3` |
| Cython 3.3.1, master (e99970f), on 3.12.13 and 3.14.6 | **`eval 2`, `eval 1`**, `2`, **`eval 4`, `eval 5`, `eval 3`**, `3` |

0.29.37 and 3.0.12 give the same output as 3.3.1.

### Expected behaviour

The arguments are evaluated from left to right, as in Python: `eval 1`, `eval 2`, `2`, `eval 3`, `eval 4`, `eval 5`, `3`.

### OS

macOS 26.5 (ARM64)

### Python version

3.12.13 and 3.14.6

### Cython version

3.3.1 and master e99970f (3.4.0a0)

### Additional context

`EarlyReplaceBuiltinCalls._optimise_min_max()` replaces the call with a chain of `CondExprNode`s ([Optimize.py#L2100-L2131](https://github.com/cython/cython/blob/e99970f9d42e7f0ccdb3578340526577df634399/Cython/Compiler/Optimize.py#L2100-L2131)). The arguments after the first are wrapped in `ResultRefNode`s, and their `EvalWithTempExprNode`s are put around the whole chain (L2128-L2129), so they are evaluated first. The first argument is only evaluated inside the first comparison, through `ResultRefNode(last_result)` (L2112-L2114).

Putting the first argument into a `ResultRefNode` as well, evaluated first, fixed it in my local test:

```diff
--- a/Cython/Compiler/Optimize.py
+++ b/Cython/Compiler/Optimize.py
@@ -2107,11 +2107,14 @@
                 # leave this to Python
                 return node
 
-        cascaded_nodes = list(map(UtilNodes.ResultRefNode, args[1:]))
-
-        last_result = args[0]
-        for arg_node in cascaded_nodes:
-            result_ref = UtilNodes.ResultRefNode(last_result)
+        # Evaluate all arguments from left to right before comparing them.
+        cascaded_nodes = list(map(UtilNodes.ResultRefNode, args))
+
+        last_result = cascaded_nodes[0]
+        for arg_node in cascaded_nodes[1:]:
+            # The first argument is already in a temp, later results are not.
+            needs_temp = last_result is not cascaded_nodes[0]
+            result_ref = UtilNodes.ResultRefNode(last_result) if needs_temp else last_result
             last_result = ExprNodes.CondExprNode(
                 arg_node.pos,
                 true_val = arg_node,
@@ -2123,7 +2126,8 @@
                     operand2 = result_ref,
                     )
                 )
-            last_result = UtilNodes.EvalWithTempExprNode(result_ref, last_result)
+            if needs_temp:
+                last_result = UtilNodes.EvalWithTempExprNode(result_ref, last_result)
 
         for ref_node in cascaded_nodes[::-1]:
             last_result = UtilNodes.EvalWithTempExprNode(ref_node, last_result)
```

With this change, the example prints the same as CPython, and the generated C for `max(a, b)` only changes the order of the temp assignments. `runtests.py` for `builtin_min_max`, `type_inference`, `memoryview`, `powop`, `ct_DEF` and `test_patma` still passes. `tests/run/builtin_min_max.pyx` has no case where more than one argument has a side effect. This looks separate from #4146, which is about a name being read after a later operand changed it.

comment_data.body: This has the feeling of "yes fine but do we really care?" In this case it's a fairly easy fix so maybe we should take it but there's almost certainly loads of these places and it feels like minutiae that's easy to generate in bulk with an LLM but it's ultimately mostly noise

title: [BUG] `max()` and `min()` with several arguments evaluate them out of order: `max(f(1), f(2))` calls `f(2)` first
